rules.instruction: When the description says the customer chooses one option from several alternatives (for example, a set of attribute values), and each chosen option is manufactured or handled by its own named party, so only the party for the chosen option must receive a request: Model an exclusive decision gateway right after the customer's choice is known and before any request is sent. Give each alternative its own outgoing sequence flow to a separate send task whose label names the party that handles that alternative, using the description's wording. Do not send one generic request covering all alternatives, and do not use a parallel gateway, because only the party for the chosen option is contacted. Join the branches again with an exclusive merge gateway before the next step.
rules.situation: the description says the customer chooses one option from several alternatives (for example, a set of attribute values), and each chosen option is manufactured or handled by its own named party, so only the party for the chosen option must receive a request

rules.instruction: When The description states an activity together with its object and a named recipient or performer (for example, items sent to one or several parties, or work done by a stated party), and the activity is to be modeled as a send, receive or manual task.: Label the task with the verb and object the description uses, and keep the stated recipient or performer in the label. If the description names several recipients or performers for the same activity, keep that whole set in the label, or model one task per recipient when they are handled separately. Do not narrow the set to a single party that the description does not name.
rules.situation: The description states an activity together with its object and a named recipient or performer (for example, items sent to one or several parties, or work done by a stated party), and the activity is to be modeled as a send, receive or manual task.

rules.instruction: When the description states that a subject may optionally request extra options, with words such as 'likes to' or 'may', that some parties must act on before shared steps continue, while the remaining steps apply to every case: Place an exclusive decision gateway after the point where the optional requests are known and before the shared steps. One outgoing flow runs the task that passes the chosen options to the parties that must act on them, then continues to the shared step. The other outgoing flow skips these tasks and goes directly to the shared step. Label the flows with the condition. Rejoin the branches with an exclusive merge gateway before the shared step. Add no gateway when every case receives the same steps.
rules.situation: the description states that a subject may optionally request extra options, with words such as 'likes to' or 'may', that some parties must act on before shared steps continue, while the remaining steps apply to every case

rules.instruction: When the description says that a producer, after collecting a customer's chosen features, sends requirements to several different named teams, each of which manufactures a different part, and every one of these teams is contacted: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow, then one separate send task for each receiving team, labeled with that team's name and the requirements it receives, as the description words them. Each send task gets its own branch. Rejoin the branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not use one generic send task that covers all teams and all parts, and do not use an exclusive gateway, because every team is contacted.
rules.situation: the description says that a producer, after collecting a customer's chosen features, sends requirements to several different named teams, each of which manufactures a different part, and every one of these teams is contacted

rules.instruction: When the description states one user action whose clause joins several distinct inputs or choices with 'and' (for example, 'provides X and Y' or 'selects A, B, and C'), followed by a further step that depends on them: Model each distinct input or choice named in that clause as its own user task, in the order the description states them, and connect these tasks in sequence before the task for the dependent step. Do not merge the items into one task, and do not leave any stated item out of the model.
rules.situation: the description lists several features that a customer chooses for a product in one sentence, separated by commas and 'and', and a later sentence sends the collected choices onward to another party that acts on them

Do not send one generic request covering all alternatives, and do not use a parallel gateway, because only the party for the selected alternative is contacted. Rejoin the branches with an exclusive merge gateway before the next step.
